title: Rabbi Huna HaKohen bar Avin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: According to Hyman, he is mentioned in Pesikta Rabbati, piska “BeYom Kallot Moshe,” section 3, 25a, speaking in Rabbi Acha’s name; in Midrash Tehillim 110:3, speaking in Rabbi Bivi’s name; in Pesikta Rabbati, piska “Anokhi Menachemkhem,” speaking in Rabbi Yosef’s name; and in Bamidbar Rabbah 7:4, speaking in the name of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman.
He is mentioned in Midrash Tehillim 107:1 and Tanchuma, Vayishlach 11 and Shemot 1.
In Pesikta Rabbati, chapter 5: Rabbi Huna HaKohen, followed by the supplied בר אביו; Hyman proposes reading bar Avin.
Hyman cites Midrash Tehillim 106: Rabbi Huna HaKohen in the name of Rabbi Avin.

Rabbi Tanchuma bar Abba was his student, as in Bamidbar Rabbah 3:7: “Rabbi Tanchuma bar Abba said: I asked and learned before Rabbi Abba Huna HaKohen son of Rabbi Avin”; Hyman identifies him as Rabbi Huna, as it concludes there: “Rabbi Huna said to him.”

notes.text: The supplied בר אביו is retained literally and Hyman’s proposed bar Avin remains an emendation. Neither Aviv nor the reviewer’s Avyo is adopted as an established proper name. The source wording remains held in p003; חהלים is read as תהלים, without a native proof claim.

In the Meir Ish-Shalom edition of Pesikta Rabbati, chapter 5, the main text reads Rabbi Huna HaKohen ben aviv (בן אביו) in the name of Rabbi Acha. Hyman prints bar aviv (בר אביו) and proposes bar Avin (בר אבין). In the consulted Midrash Tehillim 110, the report in Rabbi Bivi’s name is attributed to Rabbi Yehudah HaKohen bar Avin. The consulted Pesikta Rabbati 33 gives Rabbi Chunya HaKohen ben Avin in the name of Rabbi Yosef, immediately after a separate report by Rabbi Huna HaKohen ben Avun.

The consulted Midrash Tehillim places the report in Rabbi Avin’s name at 107:1. The inspected report by Huna HaKohen in chapter 106 is in the name of Rabbi Yirmeya in the name of Rabbi Chiyya the Great. Compare the patronymic bar Avin in Buber’s Tanchuma, Vayishlach 11 and Shemot 1, and in Bamidbar Rabbah 7:4, where the named report continues from Shmuel bar Nachman to the teachers in the Diaspora. Bamidbar Rabbah 3:7 begins the exchange with Rabbi Abba Huna HaKohen son of Rabbi Avin and later calls him Rabbi Huna, as Hyman observes.
